title: Tenant TFState silo and GPU lease coordinator module
author: Asha Kaur
release_notes: Introduce tenant-scoped TFState siloing and a new tenant GPU lease coordinator module; includes safe migration helper and docs. No breaking API changes for operators; migration required for existing TFState layouts.
description:
Background and motivation: customers running Private deployments have asked for stronger isolation between tenant state and tenant-scoped GPU pools to reduce blast radius when performing nodepool upgrades and to enable per-tenant rollback without impacting other tenants. This PR adds a tenant-scoped TFState layout (tfstate-silo module) and a tenant GPU lease coordinator module that centralizes ephemeral GPU assignment and IAM scoping for leases.

What this PR does: adds a new Terraform module modules/tfstate-silo which provides a namespaced backend prefix strategy, automated state locking keys, and a small set of helpers to stitch legacy state into the new layout; introduces modules/tenant-gpu-lease-coordinator which drives GPU subpool claims, IAM role binding templates (ephemeral lease roles), and cross-tenant network peering helpers for GPU traffic isolation; includes a migration script scripts/tfstate-migrate/warp-state.py that can perform dry-run and apply modes to replicate existing tfstate into per-tenant state blobs with validation checks.

Key files and surface changes (high level): modules/tfstate-silo/* (README, variables, backend configuration), modules/tenant-gpu-lease-coordinator/* (main.tf, iam.tf, outputs.tf, tests), scripts/tfstate-migrate/warp-state.py (migration helper), examples/private/tenant-isolation.md (operator runbook), helm/redwood-private/values-gpu.yaml (hooks to supply lease coordinator settings), ci/acceptance/private-tenant-gpu.yml (new acceptance tests that run on small infra).

Migration path and safety: The migration helper supports a two-phase workflow: (1) dry-run to produce a candidate per-tenant state and verify resource equivalence, (2) apply which creates the new per-tenant state and updates remote locks. Operators should run the migration during a maintenance window; the helper will acquire locks and surface drift warnings. A rollback flow is provided that re-binds the new state back to the legacy monolithic state if an unexpected error occurs. The PR includes a detailed example in examples/private/migration-playbook.md.

Testing and CI: Added new acceptance tests that create a minimal tenant, request a GPU lease, validate that IAM role templates are created with limited scope, verify that peering rules limit GPU traffic to tenant subnets, and then perform a controlled simulated node drain/rollout. All CI checks green on the merge commit; acceptance tests run in gating CI and in a nightly matrix for multiple cloud providers.

Security and RBAC notes: new IAM role templates are intentionally conservative (assume-role with MFA disabled for automation principals, short TTL credentials via STS). The module exposes KMS key ARNs for encrypting per-tenant state and enforces CMK key policy restrictions. Reviewers should pay attention to the iam.tf tests.

Rollout plan: staged rollout across three tenant cohorts: internal QA, early customers, full release. The TF migration helper and acceptance tests are included to reduce manual operator steps.

Related work: follows up on prior TF refactors that separated cluster-level TFState (ENG-3081) and compliments the new subnet claim controller (ENG-5122).

Notes: This is a first-pass implementation; we expect follow-ups for metrics (expose coordinator metrics to the console) and a lightweight controller implementation for on-prem scenarios.

review_comments: Liam O'Neill: Can we tighten the default IAM assume-role TTL? I recommend 15 minutes instead of 1 hour for default to reduce risk.
Asha Kaur: Good call — lowered default to 15m and made it configurable via variable 'lease_default_ttl'.
Priya Desai: Migration helper looks great. Suggest adding a --dry-validate flag that validates network attachments before applying state to avoid half-migrations.
Asha Kaur: Added --dry-validate and a set of sanity checks that validate peering routes and subnet CIDR overlap.
notes_for_ops: Operators: run scripts/tfstate-migrate/warp-state.py --dry-run followed by --apply during maintenance; ensure at most one coordinator instance is active in batch mode. If using on-prem installer, provide KMS key ARN via TF variable 'tenant_state_kms_arn'.
post_merge_actions: Create follow-up ticket ENG-4276 to expose coordinator metrics and ENG-4277 to add controller-mode operator in the installer charts. Update on-call playbook with new migration steps.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: migration can introduce drift between resources if external (non-Terraform) changes exist. Mitigation: helper does a resource equivalence check and fails fast on drift; maintainers can run the helper in dry-run repeatedly until clean. Additional mitigation: migration is opt-in per-tenant, not automatic.
operator_runbook_snippet: 1) Checkout this branch; 2) Run terraform init with backend config pointing to current monolith state; 3) Run warp-state.py --tenant <TENANT_ID> --dry-run; 4) Validate outputs and run warp-state.py --tenant <TENANT_ID> --apply; 5) Run terraform apply against new per-tenant state; 6) Monitor acceptance tests.
